children: Real estate stocks surged as odds of a rate hike in the October 27–28 Federal Open Market Committee meeting fell further.
According to the CME FedWatch tool, the probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike decreased to 15.5% from 17.7% a week ago and 55.4% a month ago.
Economists are questioning the effectiveness of rate shifts as a tool to fight inflation within an AI economy, according to a recent report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.

"AI is not sensitive to interest rates because most investors in AI expect returns of 10%, 20%, sometimes 30%," Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, reportedly said. "From this perspective, it doesn't matter if the Fed hikes 25 bps because the expected return on AI is expected to be so much higher than the level of the fed funds rate."

The rate-insensitive AI boom is leading to an economic phenomenon where rapid growth in one sector tends to lead to declines in other sectors. In this case, AI is likely draining capital and labor from sectors such as housing and automobiles, which will likely be hit harder as rates are hiked further, the economist said.
Besides, one or two more increases this year will do little to curb soaring crude oil prices or increase diesel supply, according to another report by Market Intelligence.

"There is growing concern that the Fed's conventional policy tools are not able to resolve the problems in the Middle East and probably won't do much to deter the tech investment boom given investor appetite to not be left behind," James Knightley, chief international economist at ING, told Market Intelligence in an interview.
"I don't see the Fed losing credibility here," Michael O'Rourke, chief market strategist with JonesTrading, reportedly said. "It is simply a challenging environment that lacks good options."
The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 1.15% week-over-week to 269.1 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF
The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index advanced 1.17%, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 1.15%.
Weekly Winners & Losers
CoStar Group

led the weekly advancers, adding 8.90% from the prior week to close at $32.31. The week saw RBC Capital Markets say the real estate information services company is poised to beat the Q3 earnings estimate and raise full-year financial guidance.
Host Hotels & Resorts
followed with a 5.83% advance week-over-week to $23.97.

Hotel REIT stocks were surging in a week that saw Freedom Broker initiate coverage of five major U.S. hotel stocks with Buy ratings. The lodging sector is said to have moved past the post-pandemic boom into a more normalized operating environment where growth relies on network expansion and fee generation rather than rapid, post-lockdown price hikes.
Data center REIT Equinix
led the decliners, retreating 3.91% to $985.98.
AI-related stocks and the tech sector plunged this week amid a

among investors that the AI infrastructure boom could become increasingly difficult to finance, particularly if inflation keeps interest rates elevated and customers struggle to generate sufficient returns on their investments.
Prologis
followed with a 2.89% pullback to $125.75. The stock

with third-quarter earnings that exceeded analyst expectations. The REIT updated its 2026 core FFO per share guidance to a range of $6.25 to $6.29 from $6.22 to $6.30, against the Visible Alpha consensus of $6.27.
However, net earnings attributable to common stockholders per diluted share guidance was lowered to $4.05-$4.15 from $4.40-$4.55.
Alexandria Real Estate Equities
topped the midcap losers. The stock price decreased 8.55% from the prior week to $41.62.

The office and life science and technology-focused REIT was trading lower after BMO Capital cut its recommendation on the stock to Sell equivalent, with the price target reduced to $41.00 from $48.00. The investment bank reduced its 2027 core FFO per share estimate by 26% on a yearly basis to $4.74. The downside is also expected into 2028.
Fermi
was a notable decliner, retreating 7.87% week-over-week to $3.16. The data center REIT fell amid a broader tech fallout even after

it signed a credit support agreement with AMD to support a lease for Phase 1 of its Project Matador energy and artificial intelligence facility in Texas covering 222 MW of gross power capacity, representing a key milestone toward securing project financing.
DiamondRock Hospitality
was the winner in the category, surging 6.34% from the previous week to $13.42.
The St. Joe Company

stock advanced 5.47% from the previous week to $68.41. The week saw the company say most of its hospitality, business services, and commercial properties are open for business in northwest Florida. Power has been restored to all the company's properties in the areas affected by Hurricane Isaias.
For the smallcap stocks, Summit Hotel Properties
(+7.57% W/W to $6.54), Hotel101 Global
(+5.66% W/W to $4.67), Xenia Hotels & Resorts
(+5.11% W/W to $18.94), Uniti Group
(-18.49% W/W to $5.60), Service Properties Trust
(-13.99% W/W to $6.15), and Hudson Pacific Properties
were notable movers.
